item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA—While the Dodgers await the conclusion of the three-game Wild Card Series between the Philadelphia Phillies and Atlanta Braves, they’ll have plenty of time to look over their 26-man roster before Game One of the NLDS on Saturday.
Among those players on the bubble is top prospect rookie outfielder Josue De Paual, who, after a scorching two-week stretch while Shohei Ohtani was on the injured list, saw his chances of joining Los Angeles in October skyrocket.
Much of the discussion surrounding the Dodgers’ final NLDS roster spot has centered around Josue De Paula and Dalton Rushing potentially battling it out for the final left-handed bat off the bench.
While De Paula has shown plenty during his brief time in the majors and remains a major part of the Dodgers’ future, his potential inclusion on the NLDS roster would come with a clearly defined role. Rather than expecting the top prospect to become an everyday contributor in October suddenly, Los Angeles would primarily be looking to his bat in specific situations.
“I would say if he were to make it, it would just be as a bat,” manager Dave Roberts said.
That distinction is important because De Paula’s other tools are unlikely to get much use in a postseason series. He impressed during his September stint with the Dodgers after Shohei Ohtani was placed on the 15-day injured list, receiving most of his opportunities at designated hitter and showing the elite offensive potential that initially made him one of the organization’s most intriguing prospects.
Defensively, De Paula has acknowledged he wants to improve, but that could limit his opportunities in the field against a team the Dodgers expect to contend deep into October. His speed is another tool that could theoretically give Los Angeles an advantage, but Roberts doesn’t appear interested in using him as a pinch-runner.
“For me, that’s just really not his calling card,” Roberts explained. “So as far as on the bases, I just haven’t seen enough to supplant somebody else. But I’ve seen enough with the bat.”
That leaves De Paula’s bat as the primary reason for carrying him, and there is certainly an argument for it. The Dodgers have seen enough offensively to believe he can change a game with one swing, and limiting his responsibilities would let him focus on the one area where Roberts has already expressed confidence.
Still, that doesn’t necessarily mean De Paula would see significant playing time.
The Dodgers are also considering Dalton Rushing, who returned for their final regular-season series against the San Francisco Giants and went 0-for-3 with a strikeout. Rushing’s ability to provide more versatility could factor into how Los Angeles ultimately constructs the bench, making the final decision about more than which player has the better bat.
Roberts has also indicated that the Dodgers could consider adding Hyeseong Kim to the NLDS roster, though his inclusion would likely center on his speed and defense rather than his offense.
For De Paula, then, making the roster would be a significant accomplishment in itself. But don’t confuse a roster spot with a major October role. If the Dodgers carry him into the NLDS, the plan appears to be using him selectively as a dangerous left-handed bat rather than asking the 20-year-old to take on a regular role.
Still, a lot can happen, and things rarely go according to plan, and that could very well bode in De Paula’s favor. Whether it’s an injury or a double-switch situation, De Paula could play more than a small pinch-hit appearance, but for now, that appears to be his role moving forward this season.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers get to kick back and watch as eight teams duke it out to move on to their respective League Division Series this week. The Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies will go head-to-head in the NL Wild Card Series before one of them moves on to try and topple LA.
One would think that this Dodgers team would have everything buttoned up well ahead of the NLDS, but there are still a couple of key questions to be answered.
Projecting the Dodgers' NLDS roster with Josue De Paula called upon
Catchers (2): Will Smith, Hunter Feduccia
For some reason, the Dodgers decided to carry three catchers on their Wild Card and NLDS rosters last year — Smith, Dalton Rushing, and Ben Rortvedt — but adjusted ahead of the NLCS by shedding Rushing, who received just one at-bat in the NLDS but otherwise rode the bench.
Rortvedt didn't get a start or even substitution after Game 2 of the NLDS with Smith slowly coming back from injury at the beginning of the postseason. Feduccia figures to play a similar break-glass-in-case-of-emergency role. As a lefty, he could get a start and then an early pull depending on matchups but, barring disaster, it's mostly going to be Smith's show.
Designated hitters (2): Shohei Ohtani, Josue De Paula
The Dodgers clearly want to find a way to bring De Paula with them in October, even if only as a lingering threat on their bench. They're reportedly not entertaining putting him in the outfield at all, and it's not hard to see why. Even if they're confident they'll be able to fix his defense in time, they can't afford any leakage in the postseason.
Ohtani is still shaking off the cobwebs from his 15-day IL stint. He picked up a few hits with promising exit velocity in his return against the San Diego Padres and later against the San Francisco Giants, but there are still question marks around what version of him we might see this postseason.
Infielders (6): Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, Tommy Edman, Max Muncy, Miguel Rojas, Kiké Hernández
A notable exclusion here is Hyeseong Kim. Although he's in the running to get a spot on the bench and exclusively come into games to pinch-run or for reassurances on defense, there's still a chance he doesn't make the roster if the Dodgers are set on carrying 13 pitchers. Edman and Hernández, though lacking the same speed as Kim, can still offer the same defensive versatility.
Outfielders (3): Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Teoscar Hernández
Pages might've found himself in the same boat as Ohtani, but he announced his return to the Dodgers after a month-long IL stint in a big way, hitting .333 with a 1.180 OPS, two homers, and five RBI against the Padres and Giants. No doubt Dave Roberts and Andrew Friedman breathed a massive sigh of relief.
Alex Call will be the odd man out. He was on all four of LA's playoff rosters last year and received sporadic appearances throughout the month, but that was when Michael Conforto was still on the payroll. Tucker and Hernández have certainly had their ups-and-downs this season, but the Dodgers would never seriously consider leaving them out.
Starters (4): Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal, Tyler Glasnow
There's not much to say about what's probably the best rotation going into the postseason. Snell and Glasnow have both battled injury this season but came back when the Dodgers needed them most. It might be too much to ask that any of Yamamoto, Snell, or Glasnow replicate their dominance from last year, but they'll certainly try.
Relievers: (9): Tanner Scott, Roki Sasaki, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Justin Wrobleski, Edwin Díaz, Kris Bubic, Edgardo Henriquez
Just like 2025, this is where things get dicey. The Dodgers' bullpen isn't quite as banged up or as unreliable as they were last year, but they're not the air-tight, bulletproof coterie that their combined salaries suggest they should be. Henriquez will be coming straight off of the IL to rejoin the team in the NLDS, and Díaz, Sasaki, and Scott are all woefully unpredictable.
There is some thought that the Dodgers might carry eight relievers instead of nine, to free up a spot on the position player side for a guy like Kim. In this scenario, we'll stick with them taking nine. If not, Bubic is the most obvious cut. Last one in, first one out.

item.content:encoded:
While eight teams battle it out to see who will advance to the Division Series, the Dodgers are among four teams using this time off to prepare for October baseball.
After winning an even 100 games in the regular season, the Dodgers secured a first-round bye and will await the winner of the NL Wild Card matchup between the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies. While the Dodgers continue to add the finishing touches to their postseason roster, there are some lingering questions as to which players will be a part of the team's depth chart.
21-year-old outfielder Josue De Paula made his presence known while filling in for the then-injured Shohei Ohtani, slashing .323/.500/.581 across 42 plate appearances before he was sent down to Triple-A Oklahoma City. Sonja Chen of MLB.com believes that both De Paula and utility man Hyeseong Kim can make an impact on the postseason roster, with the former being relegated to pinch-hit opportunities due to his lack of big-league experience in the outfield.
Of course, De Paula is capable of playing the corner outfield, but we only saw him play six innings in left as a Dodger. And given how important defense is in the postseason, I doubt we will see him in the field unless it's an emergency.
The month of September has given Shohei Ohtani plenty of time to prepare for his third consecutive postseason run with the Dodgers. The Dodgers still have another three days to prepare for the NLDS, and Ohtani is using this time to get his swing in the right place, per Chen.
"Everything is feeling great physically," general manager Brandon Gomes said on a Zoom call with the media on Tuesday. "The swings, once he came back, overall were in a good place. And using these five days to continue to get reps and feeling good into this series is really important. But feels like he's in a great spot."
Freddie Freeman had his power zapped in the second half of the regular season, hitting just one home run while posting a slugging percentage of .339. Freeman dealt with patellar tendonitis in his right knee, but entering the NLDS, he said that he's feeling a lot better, reports Jack Harris of the California Post.
"I truly feel good right now, physically," Freeman said on Tuesday, during a video conference with reporters ahead of the Dodgers' first pre-National League Division Series bye week workout. "So it's on me now to figure out the mechanics of the swing in the next five days. And I have all the confidence in myself that I will figure that out by [Game 1 on] Saturday."

item.content:encoded:
| MLB 포스트시즌 대진표.(사진=MLB 공식 홈페이지) |
서부지구 1위 휴스턴은 3번 시드를 받았다. 와일드카드 순위에 따라 뉴욕 양키스와 보스턴 레드삭스, 시카고 화이트삭스가 각각 4~6번 시드에 자리했다. 와일드카드시리즈(WC·3전2승제)에서는 휴스턴과 화이트삭스, 양키스와 보스턴이 맞붙는다. 휴스턴-화이트삭스전 승자는 클리블랜드, 양키스-보스턴전 승자는 탬파베이와 DS에서 격돌한다.
내셔널리그(NL)에서는 밀워키 브루어스가 전체 승률 1위로 1번 시드를 거머쥐었고, 서부지구 우승팀 로스앤젤레스(LA) 다저스가 2번 시드로 DS 직행 티켓을 확보했다. 동부지구 챔피언 애틀랜타는 3번 시드에 자리했고, 샌디에이고와 시카고 컵스, 필라델피아 필리스가 차례로 4~6번 시드를 받았다.
한국 야구팬들의 시선은 포스트시즌 엔트리 발표로 향한다. 김하성과 송성문, 김혜성의 소속팀이 모두 가을야구 진출에 성공했지만 실제 포스트시즌 출전 여부는 로스트 승선에 달렸다. 이정후가 뛰는 샌프란시스코 자이언츠는 포스트시즌 진출에 실패하면서 시즌을 마쳤다.
가장 힘겨운 시즌을 보낸 선수는 김하성이다. 올해 초 빙판길에서 넘어지며 오른손 중지를 다친 그는 부상 여파 속에 정상적인 경기력을 되찾는 데 애를 먹었다. 김하성은 이날 마이애미 말린스와의 정규시즌 최종전에서 7번 타자 유격수로 선발 출전해 2타수 무안타에 그쳤지만 볼넷 2개를 골라내고 한 차례 홈을 밟았다. 올 시즌 최종 성적은 타율 0.116, 무홈런, 9타점이다.
다저스에서 빅리그 2년 차를 보낸 김혜성은 지난 5월 말 마이너리그로 내려간 뒤 시즌 막판까지 메이저리그 무대로 돌아오지 못했다. 빅리그에서는 타율 0.259, 1홈런, 11타점, 5도루를 기록했다. 다저스가 포스트시즌에 진출했지만 김혜성이 가을야구 엔트리에 이름을 올릴지가 관건이다.
올해 MLB 포스트시즌은 오는 30일부터 다음달 2일까지 열리는 WC로 막을 올린다. DS는 10 4~11일, 리그 챔피언십시리즈(LCS·7전4승제)는 10월 12~21일 진행된다. 양대 리그 챔피언이 맞붙는 월드시리즈(7전4승제)는 다음달 24일부터 시작된다.

item.content:encoded:
[마이데일리 = 김진성 기자] “벤치의 마지막 자리는 아직 확정된 것이 아니다.”
MLB.com이 27일(이하 한국시각) LA 다저스의 디비전시리즈 로스터를 전망했다. 김혜성(27, 오클라호마시티 코메츠)이 벤치멤버 후보로 꼽혔지만, 실제로 로스터에 들 것인지 못 들 것인지에 대해선 쉽사리 얘기하지 못했다.
김혜성은 27일 막을 내린 트리플A 챔피언십서 우승을 맛봤다. 라스베이거스 에비에이터스에 2승1패로 퍼시픽코스트리그 챔피언에 올랐다. 그리고 단판으로 열린 로체스터 레드윙스와의 트리플A 챔피언십서 이기고 트리플A 챔피언에 등극했다.
김혜성은 포스트시즌 4경기서 12타수 5안타 타율 0.417 1타점 4득점 OPS 0.917을 기록했다. 물론 다다저스가 이 수치들을 그렇게 신뢰하지는 않을 것이다. 그래도 김혜성이 자신의 스타일을 살려서 시즌을 잘 마무리했다는 걸 안다.
MLB.com이 예상한 유틸리티 혹은 백업으로 포스트시즌에 포함될 선수 후보는 키케 에르난데스, 미겔 로하스, 호수헤 데 폴라, 김혜성이다. MLB.com은 “벤치의 마지막 자리는 아직 확정된 것이 아니다”라고 했다.
그러면서 MLB.com은 “다저스는 데 폴라를 데려갈 수 있지만, 달튼 러싱, 알렉스 콜, 김혜성이 추가 옵션이다. 이 결정은 잠재적인 임팩트 배트냐, 속도 및 수비력이 향상된 선수 중 누구를 벤치에 앉힐지에 달렸다. 다저스가 투수를 13명 미만으로 보유한다면, 벤치 자리가 하나 더 생기게 된다”라고 했다.
키케와 로하스는 붙박이 백업이다. 데 폴라와 러싱은 왼손 대타 용이고, 김혜성은 빠른 발로 대주자, 대수비를 할 수 있다. 콜은 대타와 외야 대수비용. 데이브 로버츠 감독이 수비와 주루를 중시한다면 김혜성을 전격 로스터에 포함할 가능성은 남아있다. 물론 그렇게 로스터에 어렵게 들어가도 실제 경기에 출전할 기회는 극히 적을 것이다.
김혜성은 트리플A 시즌을 마쳤지만, 구단들은 포스트시즌 매 스테이지마다 로스터를 변동할 수 있다. 즉, 다저스가 디비전시리즈, 챔피언십시리즈, 월드시리즈까지 치를 경우 김혜성은 꼼딱없이 귀국도 못하고 출전 대기를 해야 한다.

item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO, CA—As expected, before Game One of a three-game series against the San Francisco Giants, the Los Angeles Dodgers activated left-handed-hitting catcher Dalton Rushing from the 10-day injured list.
In order to make room on the 28-man roster, the Dodgers optioned infielder Alex Freeland to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
For Rushing, these next three games are his final chance to make his case for a spot on the Dodgers’ postseason roster. Because of his UCL injury, his role will be limited to pinch-hitting off the bench, but the second-year catcher has one last chance to show the Dodgers he can still provide an impact bat when October arrives.
This is Rushing’s second return from the injured list this month for the same injury, as the lefty lasted only eight at-bats before heading back to the IL and receiving a PRP injection to calm the pain.
In that time, while no longer on the roster due to the activation of Shohei Ohtani, the role of a left-handed hitter off the bench is also down to Josue De Paula, who posted an OPS over 1.000 and hit .323 in his short but successful stint at the major league level.
As for Alex Freeland is headed back to the Minors after joining the Dodgers when active rosters expanded on September 1st. At the time, the Dodgers opted for Freeland over an outfield prospect despite Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker both struggling, with James Tibbs III appearing to be the expected choice for that extra position-player spot.
Instead, Freeland got the call and put together a solid month, hitting .250/.413/.389 with two doubles, one home run and two RBI across 17 games, including 10 starts. He last appeared Saturday against the San Francisco Giants.
It was an inconsistent season overall for the 25-year-old, who surprisingly made the Dodgers’ Opening Day roster over Hyeseong Kim. Freeland showed flashes at both the Major League level and with Oklahoma City, and with this move, he can rejoin the Comets for their Triple-A National Championship Game in Las Vegas on Saturday.
Unfortunately for Freeland, being optioned this late in the season also closes the door on a potential postseason roster spot. He cannot be added to the Dodgers’ National League Division Series roster in time for Game One on Saturday, October 3rd, unless he replaces a player who is placed on the injured list.

The Los Angeles Dodgers activated Dalton Rushing off the 10-day injured list and optioned Alex Freeland to Triple-A Oklahoma City prior to Friday’s game against the San Francisco Giants.
Freeland heads back to the Minors after joining the Dodgers when active rosters expanded on Sept. 1. He was chosen over an outfield prospect despite Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker both struggling at the time. James Tibbs III at one point appeared to be the expected choice for the Dodgers’ extra position player.
Instead the team elected for Freeland, who hit .250/.413/.389 with two doubles, one home run and two RBI over 17 games (10 starts) this month. Freeland last played on Saturday against the San Francisco Giants.
Freeland endured an inconsistent year after making the Dodgers’ Opening Day roster over Hyeseong Kim. He had some stretches of promise not only at the Major League level, but while with the Comets as well. The 25-year-old conceivably will join Oklahoma City for their Triple-A National Championship game in Las Vegas on Saturday.
With Freeland getting optioned this late in the season, he is not a candidate to make the Dodgers’ postseason roster for the National League Division Series. He would not be eligible to get added in time for Game 1 on Saturday, Oct. 3, unless taking the spot of an injured player.
Rushing is back from a second stint on the injured list due to trouble with his right elbow. The first instance was due to a slight tear in the UCL, but the latest came because of a flexor tendon problem.
It prompted the Dodgers to halt Rushing’s throwing progression and he now has three games to seemingly make up for lost time. Rushing had been projected to be the left-handed bat off the bench for the postseason, but Josue De Paula may now have the inside track for that role.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts indicated Rushing would receive a maximum of three at-bats as a pinch-hitter this weekend.
Like Andy Pages and Shohei Ohtani earlier this week, Rushing is back without having gone on a rehab assignment in part because of the Minor League season ending. Though, he did log at-bats against Will Klein, who likewise is hopeful to earn a role with the Dodgers come October.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers will activate Dalton Rushing on Friday before their final regular-season series, giving the left-handed power hitter at least a few more days and a handful of at-bats to unleash his swing.
The Dodgers are not ruling out a possible spot on a playoff roster, but as of now, they are just focused on giving Rushing the chance to take a few swings in San Francisco in a sign of respect.
“At the most it would be three pinch-hit at-bats, so just conduct at-bats and see what you got,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “Just the circumstances of his situation, it’s just tough to just be hurt, come back, then be hurt again, and then take three pinch-hit at-bats to potentially then say, ‘Hey, you’re on the roster.’
“What he’s done for us this season certainly deserves some (playoff) consideration. That’s kind of giving him the respect and thoughtfulness of what he’s done for us.”
Rushing understands the situation and is fully on board with whatever decision is made.
His season was put in jeopardy when he went on the injured list in early August with an elbow injury that was diagnosed as a small UCL tear with a forearm flexor strain.
Determined to return as both a hitter and a catcher, Rushing worked at both sides of his game and returned on Sept. 1. But the continued throwing work outside of games led to a setback and he went back on the IL less than a week later.
“The at-bat’s really are the only side that I can truly help them in,” Rushing said Thursday. “Even then, it’s just a pinch-hit opportunity and no defense included, so I know that ties their hands up a little bit. But yeah, I’m excited.”
Without much time to make an impact, and the Dodgers also having the option of using left-handed-hitting rookie Josue De Paula on the playoff roster, Rushing is well aware of what he is up against. The club even has the option of using the lefty hitting Hyeseong Kim in the playoffs for his defense and speed.
“No hard feelings on either end,” Rushing said about getting a chance to play in the playoffs. “Obviously you want to play baseball. You feel healthy again to an extent. You feel healthy swinging a bat, so yeah, I want to get back soon.”
The next challenge is determining the extent of his elbow injury. Rushing is swinging pain-free after a platelet-rich plasma injection, but figuring out when he can throw again remains in question.
He is determined to rehab the injury, knowing that some kind of surgical procedure might be needed.
“I think as soon as we get into the offseason, that’s decision time,” Rushing said. “Progressing the way that I’m progressing right now, I’m very optimistic it is going to be totally fine and just think it was a lot of workload increase very quickly. I think that’s what sparked it. Once I got the shot, it felt really, really good.”
Roberts did not say what the full roster move will be on Friday.
VIEW FROM THE TOP
Shohei Ohtani was back in the leadoff spot on Thursday after batting second in his return from the IL on Wednesday.
While his turn as a No. 2 hitter came because the San Diego Padres had left-hander Robbie Ray on the mound, Roberts has not said if batting second against a lefty will be a regular feature of the lineup.
“I’m kind of toying with it clearly,” Roberts said. “But I’m not sure exactly whether he’s going to stick in the one or rotate him depending on the pitcher.”
Ohtani went 1 for 4 with a walk on Wednesday, but the comfort level he showed at the plate pleased Roberts.
“I hope that’s a sign of things to come,” Roberts said. “Taking the first slider from Robbie Ray for a ball, (that) got him into a good count, whereas the last couple weeks he was just hair-on-fire swinging and chasing. It’s a hard way to make a living that way, right? I thought (Wednesday) the patience was really good. I hope that’s more to come.”
CATCHING ON FAST
After starting the first two games of the series against the Padres, catcher Will Smith gave way to backup Hunter Feduccia on Thursday but was available off the bench.
Smith is also set to start two of the three games in San Francisco over the weekend before settling into an everyday role in the playoffs.
In the last five games Smith started, he was batting .421 (8 for 19) with three home runs and five RBIs. Since returning from neck inflammation on Sept. 1, he is batting .255 with four home runs and 11 RBIs in 19 games.
UP NEXT
Dodgers (LHP Tarik Skubal, 11-7, 2.85 ERA) at Giants (RHP Yunior Marte, 0-1, 4.66 ERA), Friday, 7:15 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM, 1020 AM

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- As the Dodgers mull over how to assemble their postseason bench, part of the decision may come down to weighing one small sample of plate appearances against another.
The Dodgers plan to activate Dalton Rushing from the 10-day injured list before Friday's series opener against the Giants at Oracle Park, manager Dave Roberts said Thursday. Rushing, who will only be available as a hitter due to a partial tear of the ulnar collateral ligament in his right elbow, is expected to get three pinch-hit appearances at most during the final weekend of the regular season.
Rushing has taken just eight plate appearances since the beginning of August, when he sustained the elbow injury. He spent most of August on the IL, returned when rosters expanded on Sept. 1 and went back on the IL shortly afterward when he aggravated his elbow while working through a throwing progression.
It would be an uphill battle for Rushing to make the postseason roster, Roberts acknowledged. But the Dodgers want to give the 25-year-old backstop the chance to end the season with the big league club.
"Just the circumstances of his situation, it's just tough to just be hurt, be back, then be hurt again," Roberts said. "And then take three pinch-hit at-bats, potentially, and then say, 'Hey, you're on the roster.'
"What he's done for us this season certainly deserves some consideration. That's kind of giving him the respect and thoughtfulness of what he's done for us."
The likely front-runner to be the primary left-handed bat off the bench is top prospect Josue De Paula, who was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City when Shohei Ohtani was activated from the 15-day IL on Wednesday. De Paula's career in the big leagues spans a mere 11 games and 42 plate appearances -- but he greatly impressed the Dodgers with his ability to conduct an at-bat, hitting 10-for-31 (.323) and reaching base at a .500 clip.
"He's done everything he can to put himself in a position to be in the conversation for us as we're making our postseason roster," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said.
Rushing has hardly played in the past two months, but he has a larger sample of big league plate appearances to draw on. He took a step forward in his second season in the Majors, hitting .249 with a .798 OPS and 12 homers.
So the Dodgers aren't only considering Rushing's next three plate appearances as they evaluate him for a potential bench role.
"It's a small track record, but it's a good track record," Roberts said.
Whether Rushing or De Paula best suits the Dodgers' bench needs is a more complex question. Both are essentially hitters only, Rushing due to his elbow and De Paula because his defense is a work in progress. De Paula would be a better option to run off the bench, as he swiped 30 bags in back-to-back Minor League seasons, while Rushing has never stolen more than two bases in a single professional season.
But if the Dodgers really wanted to round out their bench with a designated runner or defensive specialist, then carrying someone like Hyeseong Kim would make more sense than either Rushing or De Paula. Roberts said that he could see the team carrying 14 position players and 12 pitchers in the best-of-five NL Division Series -- opening an additional spot on the bench -- whereas in the best-of-seven NL Championship Series, the team would probably lean toward carrying the maximum 13 pitchers.
So while performance at the big league level matters, the decision will be more involved for Rushing, De Paula and the Dodgers' other postseason bench options.
"There's some nuanced conversation that needs to happen," Roberts said, "and what fits best for a potential first-round matchup."

item.content:encoded:
It was a win-or-go-home game for the Comets, and they live to fight another day after dominating the Aviators in Game 2 of the Championship Series in a 7-2 victory.
Player of the Day
While Zach Ehrhard and James Tibbs III led the way with the bat, it was Landon Knack’s outstanding work as a starter that allowed the Comets to open a five-run lead before the Aviators could think about entering the game. Doing a complete 180 from the previous game’s pitching struggles, Landon Knack didn’t walk anyone and struck out eight in 6.1 one-run innings.
For anyone closely monitoring Knack’s September stats, this was hardly a surprising development, considering he had come into the game with 11.2 scoreless innings this month, 7.2 of them in Triple-A with the Comets.
Triple-A Oklahoma City
The middle-infield combo of Noah Miller and Hyeseong Kim reached in front of Zach Ehrhard in the third inning, and the Comets’ leadoff hitter drove them both in to give his team a lead they would maintain until the end.
Between the third and fifth innings, the Comets scored six of their eventual seven runs, all unanswered, capped by a James Tibbs III three-run bomb, doing what he has done basically the whole year.
The Comets showed discipline to put the ball in play, ending the game with only five strikeouts, under half the total of the Aviators’ lineup. Ryan Fitzgerald, the veteran who was the only Comet to strike out multiple times, got on the scoreboard with a solo shot in the eighth.
Not only dominant, but Knack also found a way to be extremely efficient and could’ve easily gone further than the 6.1 innings he covered, getting the hook when he was at just 81 pitches. Recently demoted flamethrower Seth Halvorsen contributed a scoreless frame with a walk and two strikeouts. The Aviators’ second and final run came against Paul Gervase in the ninth inning.
Transactions
The Comets placed outfielder Chris Newell and pitcher Jackson Ferris on the Development List. The Dodgers optioned pitcher Kyle Hurt and outfielder Josue De Paula to the Comets. Lastly, they activated Emmet Sheehan as well.
Wednesday’s scores
- Las Vegas 2, Oklahoma City 7
Thursday’s schedule
- 7:05 p.m. PT: Oklahoma City (Cole Irvin) at Las Vegas (TBD)

item.content:encoded:
Utility player Hyeseong Kim is giving the Los Angeles Dodgers something to think about as they’re putting together the postseason roster.
Kim, who’s been with the Oklahoma City Comets since May, went 2-for-4 in Game 2 of the Pacific Coast League Championship Series Wednesday night.
Kim’s night also included a double, an RBI and a run scored in the Comets’ 7-1 win over the Las Vegas Aviators, a victory that forces a deciding Game 3 on Thursday.
It came on the heels of another 2-for-4 game for Kim on Tuesday night in which he also scored two runs, a sign of progress amid a largely uneven season at the plate.
How has Hyeseong Kim played in 2026?
Kim’s production at the major-league and minor-league levels has been virtually identical in 2026, and not in a way that shows Kim living up to his potential.
In the majors, he hit .259 with one home run and 11 RBIs.
In the minors, where he’s spent about triple the time, he is hitting .262 with three homers and 31 RBIs.
He has also stolen five bases in the majors and 15 in the minors.
While the production hasn’t necessarily been eye-popping, his skills could be a huge boon to the Dodgers in the playoffs, something manager Dave Roberts addressed recently.
What do the Dodgers plan to do with Hyeseong Kim?
Roberts said that the Dodgers plan to use next week, when they are almost assuredly going to get a bye for the wild card round, to meet with Kim and possibly add him to the postseason roster.
“My expectation is that Kim will be here during the off week and potentially be in the conversation for the postseason, because he has the ability to run and play defense and steal a base,” he said.
That said, those offensive numbers that Kim has put up in Triple-A and the majors this season give Roberts and the Dodgers coaches and executives pause, he said.
“I think for Hyeseong, it’s the at bat consistency,” Roberts said. “I don’t think that his offense has been consistent.”
Especially compared to some of the other players who are fighting for a playoff roster spot, Kim’s relative inconsistency could spell doom for his postseason hopes.
“For us, the at bat quality, for example, that Alex Freeland is giving us has been very good,” Roberts said. “He gets on base. I think for Hyeseong, just trying to find something consistent and perform consistently. And to be quite frank, he just hasn’t been as consistent as he can be. But if he can get more consistent with the bat, then he can be a big piece.”
Dodgers fans will find out in the coming days if Kim has indeed done enough to earn a spot for October, but his supporters can rest assured that he’s putting his best foot forward in these Triple-A playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Miguel Rojas has done something no other Dodger has done before.
Rojas was named the winner of the 21st annual Roy Campanella Award, the third year in a row that he’s taken the honor.
No other Dodger has won the award, which the team said is “is given to the Dodger player who best exemplifies the spirit and leadership of the late Hall of Fame catcher,” three straight years, though Justin Turner did win three awards in 2017, 2019 and 2020.
He’ll be honored before Thursday’s game by Campanella’s daughter, Joni Campanella Roan, and his granddaughter, Akua Campanella.
Why was Miguel Rojas honored with the Campanella award?
Rojas won the award through a vote by uniformed Dodgers personnel, and it makes sense given his “rock solid” performance this season.
Not only is he hitting .271 with four homers and 22 RBIs in 103 games, but he also has started at second base, shortstop and third base, racking up a .995 fielding percentage.
He also, of course, hit the game-tying home run in Game 7 of the 2025 World Series, forever stitching his name in Dodgers lore, though his on-field performance is far from all he brings to the team.
“Rojas’ excellent leadership in the clubhouse is by now common knowledge among baseball fans,” the team said in a news release. “The last four years, he’s instituted players-only, series-victory celebratory toasts in the locker room when the Dodgers take a series or record a sweep. Rojas will kick off the toasts with a few words and then throw it over to the ‘player of the game.’ He’s also famous for his mentorship of players both young and old, including Mookie Betts, Alex Freeland and Hyeseong Kim.”
What’s next for Miguel Rojas?
Rojas is expected to retire after this season, and “next year he is expected to transition into a front office job with a focus on player development,” the team said.
In the meantime, he’s soaking up what’s likely his final few weeks as an MLB player.
“I never take it for granted,” Rojas told Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez. “I feel like every opportunity we have to take this field is really special, especially after what happened the last couple of years, not just to me but to the organization and the city.”

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Dodgers announced today that infielder Miguel Rojas was named the winner of the 21st annual Roy Campanella Award, which is given to the Dodger player who best exemplifies the spirit and leadership of the late Hall of Fame catcher. The award, which was voted upon by Dodger uniformed personnel, will be presented to Rojas by Campanella’s daughter, Joni Campanella Roan, and his granddaughter, Akua Campanella, during pregame ceremonies on Thursday night.
Rojas, 37, becomes the second player to win three Campanella awards, joining Justin Turner (2017, 2019-20) and he’s the very first to win three in a row. He’s one of four players to take home the honor multiple times, along with Clayton Kershaw (2013-14), Turner and Chase Utley (2016, 2018). Rojas also becomes the second oldest player to win the award, after Utley (37, 39).
Rafael Furcal received the inaugural Roy Campanella Award in 2006 and since then the honor has been awarded to Russell Martin (2007), James Loney (2008), Juan Pierre (2009), Jamey Carroll (2010), Matt Kemp (2011), A.J. Ellis (2012), Kershaw (2013-14), Zack Greinke (2015), Utley (2016, 2018), Turner (2017, 2019-20), Chris Taylor (2021), Freddie Freeman (2022), Jason Heyward (2023) and Rojas (2024-26).
Rojas has been rock solid at the plate in 2026, hitting .271 with four homers and 22 RBI in 103 games, while batting .297 (43-for-145) vs. left-handed pitching and .287 at UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium. Defensively, he’s been as steady as ever, starting 36 games at second base (135 chances without an error), 17 at shortstop and three at third while making just one error on the season, good for a .995 fielding percentage.
In 2025, the Dodgers brought the native of Venezuela back for another season, a decision that proved pivotal this season as made starts at second base (43), third base (20) and shortstop (10), before delivering one of the biggest home runs in World Series history. In the bottom of the ninth of Game 7 vs. the Blue Jays in Toronto, his one-out solo homer off Jeff Hoffmann tied the game at 4-4, allowing Los Angeles to comeback and win its second straight World Series with a 5-4 win in extra innings.
Rojas returned to the Dodgers in 2023 and signed a two-year deal, coming back to the organization where he made his Major League debut on June 8, 2014 and as the starting third baseman, helped preserve Clayton Kershaw’s no-hitter on June 18, 2014 with a stellar play. After hitting .236 in 2023, Rojas rebounded in a big way in 2024, hitting .283 in 103 games and playing his usual Gold Glove defense all over the diamond. Rojas also provided invaluable leadership to the club last year as he played on a World Series winner for the first time that year.
Rojas’ excellent leadership in the clubhouse is by now common knowledge among baseball fans. The last four years, he’s instituted players-only, series-victory celebratory toasts in the locker room when the Dodgers take a series or record a sweep. Rojas will kick off the toasts with a few words and then throw it over to the “player of the game.” He’s also famous for his mentorship of players both young and old, including Mookie Betts, Alex Freeland and Hyeseong Kim.
The slick-fielding veteran has mentioned that 2026 might be his final Major League season and next year he is expected to transition into a front office job with a focus on player development.
After the club won the National League West last week, Rojas said of his teammates: “This is family to me. These guys kept me positive and kept me going every single day. I can’t thank the guys enough for what they have done for me the last four years. I’m so excited for the opportunity to three-peat with this team.”
Campanella was a three-time National League Most Valuable Player (1951, 1953 and 1955), eight-time All-Star and a member of the 1955 World Championship team. He played in five World Series and his 142 RBI in 1953 set a franchise record, since surpassed by Tommy Davis (153 in 1962). In 1,215 career games during a 10-year career, all with the Dodgers, he batted .276 with 242 home runs and 856 RBI.
He began his career in the Negro Leagues, establishing himself as one of the top catchers in the league before joining the Dodger organization in 1946. Campanella played for Class B Nashua of the New England League, making that club the first integrated affiliated baseball team in the United States.
On Jan. 29, 1958, just as the Dodgers were making final preparations for their move to Los Angeles, Campanella was involved in a tragic car accident that paralyzed him from the neck down, marking the end of his playing career. On May 7, 1959, a Major League record-setting 93,103 fans filled the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on “Roy Campanella Night” for an exhibition game between the Dodgers and Yankees.
He was inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 1969 and was among the first three Dodgers to have their uniform numbers retired alongside Jackie Robinson and Sandy Koufax. Campanella remained active in the Dodgers’ Community Relations Department until his death on June 26, 1993, at the age of 71.
The Los Angeles Dodgers franchise, with nine World Series championships and 26 National League pennants since its beginnings in Brooklyn in 1890, is committed to a tradition of pride and excellence. The Dodgers, baseball’s 2024 and 2025 back-to-back World Champions, are the reigning Sports Business Journal Sports Team of the Year, have been recognized as ESPN’s Sports Humanitarian Team of the Year and are dedicated to supporting a culture of winning baseball, providing a first-class, fan-friendly experience, and building a strong partnership with the community. With the highest cumulative fan attendance in Major League Baseball history and a record of breaking barriers, the Dodgers are one of the most cherished sports franchises in the world. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are still fighting to keep their first-round bye, but they're already prepping for their 14th consecutive postseason appearance — and there are a number of questions they still need to answer.
Will Shohei Ohtani be ready? Does Edwin Díaz make the roster? Will Andy Pages be available? Is Roki Sasaki ready to return to his role as the Dodgers' vaunted postseason closer?
Every option to try to make up for these weaknesses is being considered. Even Hyeseong Kim, who has spent the majority of this season at Triple-A Oklahoma City.
"My expectation is Hyeseong will be here during the off-week and potentially be a conversation for the postseason — because he has the ability to run, play defense, and steal a base," Dave Roberts said, "So he's in the conversation, yes."
Alex Freeland is probably the most dispensable player on the Dodgers' active roster. If he's left behind, it'll be proof that their second base battle never truly declared a winner.
Dave Roberts hints at Hyeseong Kim return for Dodgers' postseason run
Kim was last seen in the majors from early April to late May. He was initially called up to replace Mookie Betts who went onto the injured list with an oblique strain. Kim hit .259 with a .651 OPS before being sent back down. His numbers in Triple-A have been nothing to write home about either (.675 OPS).
But Kim was on the Dodgers' postseason roster last season. His contributions were few — he earned a pinch-running appearance in the NLDS and was a defensive substitution during the World Series — and he didn't pick up a bat.
But Freeland is hot, and is hitting .375 with a 1.149 OPS over his last seven games. His ability to get on-base, the attribute that really put him on the map to begin with, has slowly come back to him. He has a .413 on-base percentage in September.
Clearly, this is a conversation the Dodgers are going to have to continue unless they trade one or both of these players. If Kim and Freeland survive the offseason together, they'll probably have to do it all over again next year.
